A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DGQ research. All 23 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-I, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantization experiments on MS-COCO and PartiPrompts, component ablations, attention-distribution analyses and generated-image comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, distribution analyses and qualitative comparisons, including Tables 1-3 and A.1-A.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dimension selection, K-means grouping, timestep-specific quantization parameters and attention-aware quantization, including separate handling of the <start> token.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS-COCO for calibration and evaluation and PartiPrompts for prompt-generalization evaluation. The appendices retain the same data and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Q-Diffusion and TFMQ-DM for Stable Diffusion v1.4 and TFMQ-DM for SDXL Turbo. The appendix comparisons also retain their original comparator membership.

E3.justification: V2 removes Section 4.3's statement that all ablations used W8A8, correcting its conflict with the W8A6 rows already present in Table 3. This revises the protocol description; the displayed configurations remain unchanged and no reruns are established.

E4.justification: The component, grouping and attention ablations in Table 3 are unchanged. Appendices A, B and F-H retain the same token interventions, grouping sensitivity, attention analyses and activation visualizations.

E5.justification: Seed-related statements and statistical reporting are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same descriptive attention-distribution statistics, with no added run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and A.1-A.3 retain identical results, and the qualitative images are unchanged. Section 4.2 replaces the stated CLIP decreases of 0.001 and 0.004 with the consistent summary 'less than 0.005'; the underlying values remain available in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), their mathematical definitions and the attention-distribution reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: preserving activation outliers and text-image alignment, outperforming existing quantization methods, and enabling below-8-bit quantization without additional fine-tuning.

C2.justification: The explanations of outlier importance, prompt-dependent attention and grouping behavior remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations and future directions concerning weight quantization and attention quantizers.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that code is available and supplies a DGQ repository link in the abstract. The calibration, implementation, hardware and timing disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Ryu et al. (2024) is updated from its preprint citation to its ECCV publication details, representing the same work.

P1.justification: V2 lightly rewrites Section 4.2, removes redundant wording in Section 4.1, adds acknowledgements and funding information, and updates the running header to ICLR 2025 publication status. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 introduces colored hyperlinks and cross-references, adjusts contribution-list and Table 3 spacing, and changes page flow so the conclusion fits on page 10. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful code-access information and removes the inaccurate W8A8-only ablation statement, improving documentation and internal consistency. Limited prose and formatting refinements accompany these changes. The method, empirical evidence and scientific conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is modest.
